name: Question 5
problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}xy\,dx+x\,dy,$ where $C$ is parametrized by $r(t)={e}^{t}\,i+{e}^{t+1}\,j$ for $t\in [0,1]?$
worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)={e}^{t},\,y(t)={e}^{t+1}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t+1})\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i+{e}^{t+1}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}xy\,dx+x\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(xy\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{t+1}\cdot {e}^{t}+{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{3t+1}+{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Which of the following is equivalent to ∫Cxydx+xdy, where C is parametrized by r(t)=eti+et+1j for t∈[0,1]?

a
2∫01e2t+1dt
b
∫01e3t+1+e2t+1dt
c
2∫01e3t+1dt
d
∫01e5t+2dt
e
∫01e3t+e2tdt
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Along the curve, we have x(t)=et,y(t)=et+1.

The derivative of r(t) is given by

r′(t)=dxdti+dydtj=ddt(et)i+ddt(et+1)j=eti+et+1j.

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

∫Cxydx+xdy=∫01xydxdtdt+xdydtdt=∫01(xydxdt+xdydt)dt=∫01et⋅et+1⋅et+et⋅et+1dt=∫01e3t+1+e2t+1dt
